q: What does each node of a singly linked list contain?
opts: Data and a pointer to the next node
Data and pointers to the previous and next nodes
Only a pointer to the head
ansText: Data and a pointer to the next node
expl: A singly linked node stores its data plus one link to the following node (B describes a doubly linked list node).

q: Which order does a queue follow for insertion and removal?
expl: The first element inserted is removed first, like a line of people. LIFO is a stack.

q: Which extra pointer does a node of a doubly linked list have compared with a singly linked list node?
opts: A pointer to the middle node
A pointer to the previous node
A pointer to the data type
ansText: A pointer to the previous node
expl: Doubly linked nodes keep prev AND next, so traversal works in both directions (see the recent-files program).

q: In a circular singly linked list, where does the next pointer of the last node point?
expl: The last node links back to the head, forming a ring (that is why the walk-around program can loop using while (temp->next != head)).

q: What is the time complexity of inserting a node at the beginning of a singly linked list when the head pointer is available?
expl: Only a few pointer assignments are needed - no traversal - so it is constant time. Inserting at the END without a tail pointer is O(n) (must walk the whole list).

q: In a linked list implementation of a queue, where is a new element inserted?
opts: At a position chosen by its value
expl: Queues are FIFO: insert at the rear, remove from the front. Keeping both a front and a rear pointer makes both operations O(1).

q: Which of the following is an application of a queue?
expl: Waiting processes are served in arrival order -> a queue. B, C and D are STACK applications (last in, first out).

q: In a priority queue, which element is removed first?
opts: The element with the highest priority
ansText: The element with the highest priority
expl: Priority queues serve by importance, not by age (in a min-heap the smallest number = most urgent is served first).

q: Which stack operation adds an element to the top of the stack?
expl: push adds on top, pop removes from the top, peek only looks at the top, enqueue belongs to queues.

q: Which problem of a simple array-based queue is solved by a circular queue?
opts: Wasted space at the front after dequeues
ansText: Wasted space at the front after dequeues
expl: In a linear array the freed front cells can never be reused, so the array fills up early. The circular queue reuses them with the modulo trick rear = (rear + 1) % capacity.

q: What is the postfix form of the infix expression A * B + C?
expl: * has higher precedence than +, so A B * is done first, then + C: the operators are written right after their operands.
others: ABC*+ would mean A * (B + C) - a classic trap.

q: While evaluating a postfix expression with a stack, what is done when an operator is encountered?
opts: It is pushed onto the stack
It is added to the output string
Two operands are popped, the operation is applied and the result is pushed
ansText: Two operands are popped, the operation is applied and the result is pushed
expl: Operands are pushed; when an operator arrives, pop b then pop a (order matters for - and /), compute a op b, push the result back.

q: In infix to postfix conversion, what is done when a closing parenthesis is encountered?
opts: The parenthesis is pushed onto the stack
Operators are popped to the output until the matching opening parenthesis is reached
All operands are popped from the stack
ansText: Operators are popped to the output until the matching opening parenthesis is reached
expl: Both the closing and the opening parenthesis are then discarded - they never appear in the postfix output.

q: In a singly linked list implementation of a stack, where should push and pop take place to get O(1) time?
opts: At the end of the list with no tail pointer
In the middle of the list
At the head of the list
At a node chosen by value
ansText: At the head of the list
expl: Push and pop at the head are just a couple of pointer changes (O(1)). Working at the end without a tail pointer needs a full traversal (O(n)).
